name: turing_machine
evidence: by simulation only: a binary conservative reversible partitioned CA builds any laid-out circuit (cite:margolus-1984, run here as E-CMP-0006) and any machine becomes reversible by keeping a history (cite:bennett-1973); prior non-M1 constructions E-CMP-0011 and E-CMP-0022; from M1 rules alone M6 (E-CMP-0057) built no universal construction: the 24 species-conserving cells predict in logspace (universal with polynomial overhead only if P = L; none from finite starts on the line) and the 32 reactive cells show no zero test within width-3 species

name: lambda_calculus
evidence: lambda-definable equals Turing-computable (cite:turing-1937) so it is reached by the same circuit simulation as row 1 (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973); terms live in a laid-out encoding and beta reduction erases so a history is kept

name: combinatory_logic
evidence: S and K are equivalent to the lambda calculus (cite:curry-1958) so the row 2 simulation applies (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973); K discards its second argument so a history is kept

name: register_and_counter_machines
evidence: two counters suffice (cite:minsky-1967) and a counter can be a particle separation so no cell needs unbounded state; a laid-out register machine already runs on other repo rules (E-CMP-0005 and E-CMP-0010) and a reversible two-counter machine is universal (cite:morita-1996) so no history is needed; with M1 rules alone M6 (E-CMP-0057) found a register as a particle position (id.CBA.swap on the vacuum, ADD and SUB exact) that no mover can read, so no zero test, in every species-conserving cell a logspace prediction (efficient universality only if P = L) and on the line no universality from finite starts, and no zero test in the reactive cells within width-3 species: the verdict rests on the non-M1 constructions

name: mu_recursive_functions
evidence: mu-recursive equals Turing-computable (cite:kleene-1936) so only through the row 1 simulation (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973); minimization searches without bound and erases

name: post_machines
evidence: Post's formulation is equivalent to Turing machines (cite:post-1936) so the row 1 simulation applies (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: post_canonical_systems
evidence: canonical systems generate every recursively enumerable set (cite:post-1943); a deterministic mesh can only enumerate derivations in a fixed order through the row 1 simulation (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973), never choose one

name: markov_algorithms
evidence: normal algorithms are Turing-equivalent (cite:markov-1954); the ordered first-match substitution needs a global scan so only the row 1 simulation reaches it (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: random_access_machines
evidence: a RAM is polynomially equivalent to a Turing machine (cite:cook-1973) so it is reached through the row 1 simulation (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973); addressing is nonlocal and costs routing time on the mesh

name: random_access_stored_program_machines
evidence: the stored-program RAM is equivalent to the RAM (cite:elgot-1964) so row 9 applies (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973); the mesh has no program-memory split so the program is part of the laid-out state

name: stack_machines
evidence: two stacks simulate a tape (cite:minsky-1967) so the row 1 simulation applies (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973); pop discards so a history is kept

name: queue_machines
evidence: a queue machine is a tag system and tag systems are universal (cite:cocke-1964) so the row 1 simulation applies (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: pointer_machines
evidence: storage modification machines are real-time equivalent to other universal models (cite:schonhage-1980) and reached by the row 1 simulation (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973); the mesh links are fixed so pointers are encoded in state

name: godel_general_recursive_functions
evidence: general recursive equals Turing-computable (cite:kleene-1936) so only through the row 1 simulation (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: finite_state_automata
evidence: a fixed reversible rule on a closed finite quotient is already an autonomous finite permutation automaton whose orbits all cycle (E-CMP-0018: a finite reversible box never erases for good); reading input needs a stream from outside and a many-to-one transition needs a history (cite:bennett-1973)

name: tag_and_cyclic_tag_systems
evidence: cyclic tag systems are universal and Rule 110 emulates them (cite:cook-2004); deletion erases so on a conserving rule only the row 1 simulation reaches them (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: interaction_nets
evidence: interaction nets rewrite their own wiring (cite:lafont-1990) and the mesh's links never change, so the net is encoded in state and run through the row 1 simulation (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973); a content-free graph rewrite in the repo grows a geometry but not the dock (E-FND-0151)

name: lindenmayer_systems
evidence: parallel rewriting with insertion (cite:lindenmayer-1968) needs room the fixed mesh must make by shifting, which only a laid-out simulation does (cite:margolus-1984); growth on the mesh itself is the self-reproduction question of M10

name: pushdown_automata
evidence: recognizes the context-free languages (cite:hopcroft-1979); a stack is a laid-out row of cells that the row 1 simulation drives (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973) with the input fed from outside

name: linear_bounded_automata
evidence: bounded-space computation is a closed finite box, and deterministic space equals reversible space (cite:lange-2000) so no history space is needed; the nondeterministic machine (cite:kuroda-1964) is reached deterministically in squared space (cite:savitch-1970); M4 holds trits in place in such boxes (a 4-slot register kept forever at spacing 2 on every closed quotient for two classes) and finds moving writes recurring there as delay lines (157 of 204 within 512 rounds on the quotients; every one must in time, the box being finite) (E-CMP-0051), but runs no automaton

name: tree_automata
evidence: bottom-up tree automata (cite:thatcher-1968) need a tree, and the hyperbolic tilings carry a Fibonacci spanning tree (cite:margenstern-2008; built here in E-CMP-0001), so the input tree is a laid-out subtree and the states move by the row 1 simulation

name: term_rewriting_systems
evidence: term rewriting is Turing-complete (cite:baader-1998) and a fixed reduction strategy makes it deterministic, reached through the row 1 simulation (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: graph_rewriting_systems
evidence: graph grammars are universal (cite:rozenberg-1997) but rewrite topology the mesh holds fixed, so the graph is encoded in state and simulated (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973); E-FND-0151 found that a content-free graph rewrite does not give the dock

name: semi_thue_systems
evidence: the word problem is undecidable so string replacement is universal (cite:post-1947); a deterministic mesh enumerates rewrites in a fixed order through the row 1 simulation (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: abstract_rewriting_systems
evidence: the global map of any fixed rule is a deterministic abstract rewriting system, but a general reduction relation need not be effectively given (cite:baader-1998), so what part of the class the mesh reaches is not yet stated sharply

name: interaction_combinators
evidence: three agents and six rules are universal (cite:lafont-1997) but each rule rewires the net, which the fixed mesh does only by encoding the net in state and simulating it (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: abstract_state_machines
evidence: sequential ASMs capture every sequential algorithm step for step (cite:gurevich-2000); their first-order structures are encoded in state and run by the row 1 simulation (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: multiset_rewriting
evidence: plain multiset rewriting is a Petri net with decidable reachability (cite:mayr-1981); a charge-conserving collision of particles meeting on the mesh is a multiset rewrite (E-FND-0013 conserves charge reversibly), but the well-mixed random choice of which pair reacts is replaced by a fixed schedule and deterministic mixing

name: tile_rewriting_systems
evidence: a rule rewriting tile states is a local update the mesh already does, but rewriting tile shapes changes the geometry the base holds fixed; which reading the source means, and whether shape rewriting emerges, is open

name: cellular_automata
evidence: a reversible pair rule on a graph runs only color by color over matchings (decision 002), and the repo's knit runs as a cellular automaton bit for bit on boxes and on the unbounded mesh (E-CMP-0015; E-FND-0013); composed over one schedule period a partitioned rule is a CA with a larger neighborhood (cite:toffoli-1987)

name: rule_110
evidence: Rule 110 is weakly universal on a periodic background (cite:cook-2004) and irreversible, so a conserving reversible rule reaches it only by keeping its history one dimension up (cite:toffoli-1977); E-CMP-0011 builds it from a signed-majority rule that is not an M1 rule

name: hyperbolic_cellular_automata
evidence: weakly universal CAs exist on the pentagrid and heptagrid (cite:margenstern-2008), the repo runs a railway CA on {7,3} and {5,4} (E-CMP-0022) and shows the heptagrid prerequisites (E-CMP-0001); a pair rule needs a matching schedule there (decision 002) and curvature claims need the degree-matched control (decision 001)

name: billiard_ball_computing
evidence: the billiard-ball CA is binary, conservative, reversible and universal on the Margolus partition (cite:margolus-1984; cite:fredkin-1982), the repo runs it on the flat {4,3,4} cusp (E-CMP-0006), and the knit is conservative reversible logic (E-FND-0030); the partition is a schedule and the mirrors are a laid-out circuit

name: railway_computing
evidence: Margenstern's railway runs register machines on {7,3} and {5,4} (cite:margenstern-2008; repo E-CMP-0021 and E-CMP-0022), but the railway CA is irreversible and is not an M1 rule (plan.md 9), so on the conserving mesh it needs the track layout and a history; M6 tests it

name: wang_tiles
evidence: every run of a local rule is a valid tiling of space-time, but Wang tiling asks whether some tiling exists, which is undecidable (cite:berger-1966); the mesh runs one history and does no search, so whether constraint satisfaction emerges by relaxation is open

name: game_of_life
evidence: Life is universal (cite:berlekamp-1982) and irreversible, so a conserving reversible rule reaches it only with its history kept one dimension up (cite:toffoli-1977); E-CMP-0011 shows cusp Life with a rule that is not an M1 rule

name: reversible_cellular_automata
evidence: reversible CAs can be universal (cite:morita-1989); the 24 conservative ternary pair rules run as reversible CAs on the line (E-CMP-0025) and on every lab tiling and closed quotient (E-CMP-0027), every round a bijection whose inverse round restores the start, but only under a matching schedule (their synchronous update is not reversible, decision 002), and the 16 rules that create from the vacuum also need an orientation per matched edge

name: partitioned_cellular_automata
evidence: a partitioned CA is reversible exactly when its block map is a bijection (cite:morita-1989), which is what the conservative pair rules are; partitioned by matchings they run on the line (E-CMP-0025, a two-color and a period-3 brick schedule) and on all twelve lab geometries, open and closed (E-CMP-0027: greedy edge colorings of the closed quotients, generator, step-parity and lifted colorings of the infinite tilings on the open windows, several colorings per tiling, each in two color orders), with the Margolus partition (E-CMP-0006) and the knit's schedule phase (E-CMP-0016) as earlier cases; the partition is a declared schedule and the creating rules need an orientation (decision 002)

name: asynchronous_cellular_automata
evidence: an asynchronous CA simulates a synchronous one with extra states (cite:nakamura-1974); random update order is excluded at the base, so the mesh can only stand a fixed sequential schedule in for it, which the matching schedule of decision 002 already is (E-CMP-0016)

name: probabilistic_cellular_automata
evidence: true randomness contradicts base:deterministic; a deterministic chaotic stand-in would be emerges_with_structure (deterministic_surrogate), and E-FRC-0092 shows deterministic reversible dynamics reproducing a heatbath elsewhere, which M2-B tests for this class

name: continuous_cellular_automata
evidence: real-valued cell states contradict base:discrete_state; a continuous field read off ternary cells by averaging is the coarse-graining question of M11 (E-FLD-0031 shows such fields for the knit)

name: lenia
evidence: continuous states, space and time contradict base:discrete_state (cite:chan-2019); only a coarse-grained reading of a discrete rule could resemble it, tested under M11

name: neural_cellular_automata
evidence: real-valued states and a rule fitted by gradient descent (cite:mordvintsev-2020) contradict base:discrete_state; a discrete adaptive analogue belongs to M10

name: lattice_gas_automata
evidence: the knit is a lattice gas on the 24-direction coin that conserves charge and momentum reversibly (E-FND-0013; E-SBT-0011) with the F4 symmetry the FCHC gas needs (E-GMT-0026; cite:frisch-1986); the charge-conserving pair rules are reversible lattice gases on every lab tiling (E-CMP-0027): the full swap streams excitations ballistically through each other on the line and on ten of the eleven open tilings under each base schedule (on {3,6} its colored schedule closes a lone excitation into a period-2 orbit round one hexagon, read as confined; under a second lifted coloring {3,6} reads ballistic and {6,3} unresolved, so the full swap measures the schedule, not the rule), and the scattering classes conserve charge exactly at every collision; propagate and collide are two phases of a schedule

name: lattice_boltzmann_systems
evidence: the distributions are real-valued, so not at the base, but the knit's own lattice Boltzmann equation predicts its transport with no fitted number (E-FLD-0030) and follows it flow by flow (E-FLD-0031): it emerges as the averaged description, which is a readout outside the rule

name: langtons_ant
evidence: the ant is universal (cite:gajardo-2002) and its dynamics are reversible, so no history is needed, but its heading and the cell color exceed three states and are encoded in blocks of cells; a native ant would be a moving particle of M3

name: turmites
evidence: turmites generalize the ant (cite:gajardo-2002) and most are irreversible, so on the conserving mesh they need a block encoding and a kept history (cite:toffoli-1977)

name: wireworld
evidence: Wireworld is a four-state irreversible CA, so a conserving reversible rule reaches it only one dimension up with its history (cite:toffoli-1977); its wires and gates correspond to the laid-out billiard-ball circuits of row 33 (cite:margolus-1984; E-CMP-0006)

name: collision_based_computing
evidence: logic from colliding localized patterns (cite:adamatzky-2002) is what the billiard-ball CA does (cite:margolus-1984; E-CMP-0006); whether M1 rules carry particles with a usable collision table is M3 and M5

name: signal_machines
evidence: signal machines abstract CA signals to real positions (cite:durand-lose-2005); the discrete fragment with rational speeds and finitely many collisions is mesh particles at fixed speeds, while Zeno accumulations are excluded by base finite steps

name: cellular_graph_automata
evidence: a CA on any graph is the mesh's own form (cite:rosenstiehl-1972; run on {7,3} and {5,4} in E-CMP-0022), but on a general graph a pair rule needs a matching schedule and, unless it commutes with the swap, an orientation per edge (decision 002); an arbitrary graph other than a tiling must be laid out

name: sandpile_automata
evidence: the abelian sandpile is universal (cite:goles-1997) and its result is independent of toppling order (cite:bak-1987), but toppling is irreversible and heights exceed three states, so it needs block-encoded heights and a kept history or the open ball's outward sink

name: dynamic_graph_automata
evidence: evolving connectivity is graph rewriting (cite:rozenberg-1997), and the base mesh never rewires, so links are encoded in state and simulated as in row 23 (cite:margolus-1984); link states of their own would be new base structure

name: amorphous_computing
evidence: amorphous computing relies on randomly placed asynchronous processors to break symmetry (cite:abelson-2000); the mesh is regular and deterministic, and whether a fixed rule breaks symmetry by itself, as boundaries in M9 would, is open

name: modular_robotic_computing
evidence: modules moving on a lattice are conserved particles relocating, which the mesh carries, but computing by reconfiguring a body is the self-reproduction and construction question of M10, open
